newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA SAYS SACCHI BEING LEFT BEHIND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA SAYS SACCHI BEING LEFT BEHIND.

text.p: Gianfranco Zola believes the complicated tactics supported by coaches such as AC Milan's Arrigo Sacchi are becoming unfashionable.
"The trend is changing," the Chelsea player was reported as saying in Friday's Italian newspapers. "There's a return to the past."

"Sacchi's football, the kind that he exported and preached, has become abruptly reassessed. A general about-turn, that affects not only AC Milan," he said of the former Italy coach known for rigid zonal play and elaborate schemes.

Zola, who played regularly under Sacchi as a pillar of Italy's team, said Italy had changed under coach Cesare Maldini and other clubs were also showing signs of a return to the traditional tactics of teams of old.

"The national team is under Maldini, Lazio has swapped (coach Zdenek) Zeman for (Dino) Zoff and it seems to me that even Inter intend to go back to the old style, looking at a traditional coach like (Luigi) Simoni," he said.
Internazionale coach Roy Hodgson is leaving at the end of the season to join Blackburn in the English premier league.

Zola also had some advice for Roberto Baggio. The World Cup player, who has become increasingly frustrated at being left on the bench by Sacchi, was quoted earlier in the week as saying he knew he was wasting time but that he had no alternative to waiting.
Zola said that Baggio should consider a move to Napoli, the club where the Chelsea player made his name alongside Diego Maradona, because it was a club that appreciated talent.
"If Baggio needs warmth, if he wants to regain enthusiasm, I recommend Napoli," Zola was quoted as saying.

"He would never feel alone at Napoli. The warmth and affection of the fans would help him get over the difficult moments. And then as you know, the Neapolitans have a soft spot for talented players like Roberto."
